why.primary_action_salience: 512A and E597 use a single accent color (violet) only on the send button, so it reads as the one clear primary action; E740 also colors the 'Edit' label violet, so two elements compete for attention and the orange send button no longer stands alone as clearly.
why.control_visibility: All three keep the same Cancel/Edit/Send positions and are equally findable; 512A and E597 style Cancel and Edit identically (plain gray text) which makes their equal, secondary status obvious, while E740's colored Edit label blurs that secondary-vs-primary read even though Edit itself is easier to spot.
why.visual_craft: 512A and E597 are visually indistinguishable to me in spacing, alignment, type sizes and button proportions - I could not find a craft difference between them; E740 shares the identical layout/spacing and differs only in the button/label color choices, which read as slightly less cohesive since two different accent hues appear instead of one.
why.semantic_colour: The card explicitly warns the action leaves the app and reaches other people ('外部に出る' shown as an amber/caution-style tag), so an amber/orange send button (E740) semantically echoes that caution, whereas the violet send button in 512A/E597 is a neutral brand color that does not signal 'goes outside, be careful' any more than a routine confirm would.
why.overall: 512A and E597 have the cleaner, more conventional hierarchy (one accent color, one obvious primary action) and I could not find any visual difference between the two of them; E740 trades some of that clarity for a send-button color that arguably fits the external/caution meaning of the action better, but the extra violet on Edit muddies its own hierarchy enough that I'd still rank it third overall.

differences: Send button ('送る') is violet/purple in 512A and E597, but amber/orange in E740
'Edit' label is plain gray in 512A and E597, but colored violet/purple in E740

No other visible differences: header ('# Slack 外部に出る'), title, 宛先/差出人 fields, message body text, footer metadata ('週次同期・田中・10:42'), spacing, alignment, and typography all appear identical across all three images
